Results.ReviewText: Bought 2/2021 because my hand held had died and price was right.  Didn't need till spring and after putting together, no power when trigger pulled.  Would idle, then die.  No help from Badger in Canada, and no US repair including not on HD's repair list under warranty.  Tried to return back in April and was told only 30 day return even though it says 90 days for Badger return on website.  Currently it will not even start at all.  Been back and forth with Badger Canada and no help from them...Last response they sent me a tool to adjust something but no explanation on how as I had requested.  6 yr guarrantee is useless if there's no local place to take it, and not even any in the USA.  Has not blown one leaf.  When it did start, once you asked for more power, it died.  I read all the reviews before I purchased this, so I must be stuck with a "Lemon".  No one wants to solve the problem, not HD, and not Badger.  DO NOT BUY and certainly if you don't intend to open and made sure it works as you will be stuck too!  Very disappointed with Home Depot for selling a product with a useless warranty, and not allowing me to return it last spring.

Results.ReviewText: We got the BADGER Super-Duty 190 MPH 550 CFM 43 cc Gas Full Crank 2-Cycle Back Pack Leaf Blower to replace our old tired backpack blower that was duct taped together. It only took a few minutes to assemble and was very easy to assemble. It came with all the tools needed to assemble it. The shaft is made of 4 pieces that lock together but they also have a screw to keep them together. They have hose clamps to attach the flexible part of the hose to the shaft. The assembled unit is lightweight considering what it is. The shoulder straps and back pad are nicely padded without being super bulky. Even after doing a large area it was still comfortable and not hurting my back. The motor seems to be sitting on a spring like base so the vibration does not really transfer to your body as you work. After the initial 10 priming pumps the unit started right up within about 3 pulls. The priming system has 2 hoses that are easy to see through and keep it from flooding the engine. Since then it starts up equally as quick. It has a lock to hold the trigger so that you do not have to constantly hold it on. While in this position if you have it in a lower speed and you need more you can increase the speed by pulling the trigger but then when you let go it will resume what you have the trigger locked at. This is great if you have hand issues and saves the pain of hand fatigue after doing a large area. The handle is also able to be adjusted to accommodate different arm lengths as well as some side to side adjustment. The fuel tank is easy to access and see how the fuel level is. It is a 50:1 ratio in which we used a premixed product that was utilized by the blower well. As weird as this may seem it also appears to be fuel efficient compared to my old blower as 32 ounces has lasted a long time. After about 3 hours of blowing it was still going as strong as it did at the start with no signs of overheating. It had plenty of power to move a large pile of acorns from one spot to another. The only thing I do want to check into is an electric starting attachment so that if my mother in law decides to do the blowing it she does not have to pull start it.

The backpack frame is made from high-impact nylon, keeping durability and comfort in the design. The engine is isolated on vibration killing shock absorbers while the durable frame has ballistic nylon, fully adjustable padded shoulder straps, and a cushioned back pad mounted to it. The air tube is just a touch over 5 feet, ensuring you can deliver that blast of air up close and personal while using your user adjustable throttle control.
